business_model.answer: Freemium: a free tier (3 items) and Premium at $99.99/year, plus enterprise partnerships where financial advisors or partner providers invite clients. Acquired by Precoa in October 2024; no funding or price figure was found.

who_uses_who_pays.answer: Individuals and households organizing their own documents use it; people they trust get access. Users pay for Premium themselves, or reach Premium through an invitation from a financial advisor or partner; who pays in that case is not stated.

cost.answer: Free (up to 3 items) or Premium $99.99 a year (unlimited items, premium checklists, secure sharing). A Household Membership is mentioned without a price.

how_they_differentiate.answer: They claim to organize all of a person's life details for them and tell them what to do next, using a smart, algorithm-led planning system.

evidence.quote: Everplans organizes the details of your life for you, and keeps you one step ahead of what you need to do next.
Let our smart planning system guide your next step

unique_value_proposition.answer: Keep every important document and decision of your life in one safe place you can share with the people who will need it.

evidence.quote: All the pieces of your world in one place
Everplans helps you organize, store, and securely share all of your most important information.

retain_customers.answer: The free tier stops at 3 items, so serious use needs Premium; reminders about important dates and a content library bring people back. Cancellation terms are not stated.

evidence.quote: Store up to 3 items
Add unlimited items to your Everplan

customer_experience.answer: Self-serve: FAQs, a help center and contact form, plus articles, videos and checklists. They stress they are not doctors, lawyers or financial advisors.

evidence.quote: Access informative articles, videos,
please contact us through our help center at
Everplans is not a licensed healthcare provider, medical professional, law firm, or financial advisory firm

relatives_joining.answer: Yes. The owner names 'Read or Write Access Deputies' with permission for only chosen sections, can mark sections to open only after death (unlocked by a named 'Unlocker'), and a Household Membership adds Co-Administrators with full edit rights.

evidence.quote: including the permissions you set that give any particular Read Or Write Access Deputy access to only certain designated portions of your Everplan
you may designate one of your Read or Write Access Deputies as an “Unlocker” of your “After Death Sections.”
Co-Administrators can equally view, edit, and administrate all parts of the Everplan that you are using.

privacy_data_consent.answer: Health, financial and legal details are encrypted and, they say, not readable by staff day to day; shared only with deputies the owner chooses; stored with a HIPAA-compliant host. The owner deletes the account with a self-serve button, but other personal (non-secure) information may be kept afterward.

evidence.quote: have access to the content or details of any Secure Information you privately submit through the Services because it is encrypted
your Secure Information is stored in a HIPAA-compliant hosting provider
When you delete your account, all of your Secure Information will be deleted or (if applicable) transferred to a Co-Administrator.
Please note that we may keep your Non-Personal Information and any of your Personal Information other than your Secure Information even after your account deletion.

emergencies.answer: No emergency service or support hours are stated. The nearest thing is the after-death release of chosen sections to deputies; they also disclaim liability if data is lost or breached.

evidence.quote: the Unlocker will be able to alert Everplans that you have been “Declared Dead” through their use of the Services

setup.answer: The person signs up on the web or the mobile app (iOS, now also Android) and fills in their Everplan, guided by the planning system. Time needed is not stated.
